description:
FOUND s459am while fixing #814.  With the regexg row honest again, `strcat`
is the next row whose big-minus-small subtraction is mostly noise: perl(s)
reads 0.0014-0.0021 s across runs while BOTH runs pay ~1 s to compile the
program at load, and the measured run-to-run spread of that constant term is
up to 0.09 s.  So the ratio printed for strcat (1.78x-2.13x observed in one
session) is not a measurement of anything, it is the sign of a difference of
two noisy numbers that happens to be positive.
NOT a crash (that was #814/#880) and NOT urgent: the row is merely
uninformative, not misleading in the "attractively fast" direction, and the
verification pass added in s459am would catch it if it ever became a crash.
FIX: raise N_big until perl(s) is >= ~0.3 s (100_000 -> ~5_000_000 by the
observed slope), then re-baseline the row.  Do it when someone next wants a
strcat number; note in the commit that the row's history is not comparable
across the change, exactly as regexg's is not.
The general rule now written into tools/bench-exec.pl's header: N_big must
make the row's own work large against the constant term.  Worth one pass over
every row against that rule.


DONE s461aq: N_big 100_000 -> 20_000_000, with the reason in the row's own
comment.  MEASURED before: perl 0.0028 s / PCL 0.0050 s â both far under the
run-to-run spread of the ~1 s constant term both runs pay to compile the
program, which is why the row printed 1.00x, 1.64x and 1.79x in three
consecutive runs of the SAME two trees.  After: perl 0.3001 s / PCL 0.6633 s
/ 2.21x â an honest (losing) number where there was noise.  Same rule regexg
was fixed under (#814).
